bug.title: Multi-Page Retrieval Failure — RAG only indexes/retrieves Page 1 content
bug.impact: Users cannot access ~70-80% of policy content (anything beyond Page 1)
bug.description: The chatbot only searches or matches keywords from sections appearing on Page 1 of policy documents. Content on subsequent pages is either not parsed, not chunked, not embedded, or not indexed. This renders the majority of each policy invisible to the retrieval system.

root_cause_analysis.probable_cause: The PDF ingestion pipeline is truncating document content at Page 1 boundary. This could occur at any of three stages:

investigation_checklist.check: Verify the PDF text extraction function returns content from ALL pages. Common failure modes: - PyPDF2/PyMuPDF: using page_index=0 only instead of iterating all pages - Azure Document Intelligence: page_range parameter limiting to first page - pdfplumber: opening but only reading pages[0] Test: Run parser independently on HR-C 06.00 and print page count + text per page.

Verify the text splitter receives the full multi-page text. Common failure modes: - Concatenation bug: only first page string passed to chunker - Page metadata assignment: all chunks tagged as "Page 1" regardless of source Test: Log input length to chunker; compare against full PDF text length.

Verify all chunks are actually written to the vector store. Common failure modes: - Batch upsert silently dropping chunks beyond a limit - Deduplication logic incorrectly merging chunks Test: Count chunks in vector store per document; compare against expected count.

Verify the retrieval query does not filter results to Page 1 only. Common failure modes: - Metadata filter: page_number == 1 hardcoded in retrieval - top_k too low: only 1-2 chunks returned, all from Page 1 due to title match Test: Query vector store directly (bypass chatbot) for Page 2+ content.

fix.action: Ensure PDF parser iterates ALL pages and returns concatenated or per-page text with page numbers
fix.pseudocode: for page_num, page in enumerate(pdf.pages): text = page.extract_text() chunks = text_splitter.split(text) for chunk in chunks: chunk.metadata["page_number"] = page_num + 1 chunk.metadata["policy_number"] = extract_policy_number(filename) chunk.metadata["policy_title"] = extract_policy_title(text, filename)
fix.verification: Parser outputs text from all pages; character count matches full PDF

fix.action: Attach correct page_number metadata to each chunk based on source page
fix.verification: Each chunk in vector store has accurate page_number metadata

fix.action: Re-index all 8 test documents after parser fix; verify chunk counts
fix.verification: Vector store contains chunks from every page of every document

root_cause_analysis.probable_cause: Policy numbers (e.g., "HR-C 05.00") are not stored as searchable metadata fields in the vector index. The embedding of body text may not contain the policy number prominently enough for semantic similarity to surface it. Additionally, the retrieval query has no preprocessing to detect policy number patterns and apply targeted metadata filtering.

investigation_checklist.check: Inspect vector store schema: does a "policy_number" field exist? If not, this is the root cause.
Check if policy numbers are extracted during PDF ingestion. Likely source: PDF filename (e.g., "HR-C 05.00 Shift Differentials...pdf") or document header on Page 1.
Check if query preprocessing detects policy number patterns. Without a metadata filter, "HR-C 05.00" is treated as a semantic query and may not match any embedded text closely enough.

fix.action: Add policy_number as a filterable string field in the vector store schema
fix.schema_addition: field: policy_number type: string (filterable, not tokenized) example_values: "HR-C 05.00", "HR-E 03.00", "HR-A 01.00"

fix.action: Extract policy_number from filename or document header using regex during PDF ingestion
fix.source_priority: 1. Filename, 2. Page 1 header text, 3. Manual mapping table
fix.verification: Every chunk in the index has a non-null policy_number metadata field

fix.action: Add policy number detection to query preprocessing; when detected, apply metadata filter before or alongside semantic search
fix.logic: 1. Regex scan user query for policy number pattern 2. If found: filter vector store by policy_number == detected_value 3. Then run semantic search within filtered results 4. If no results: fall back to unfiltered semantic search
fix.verification: Query "HR-C 05.00" triggers metadata filter and returns correct policy

bug.title: Punctuation-Sensitive Matching — Commas/semicolons in titles break partial keyword search
bug.impact: Inconsistent search experience; users must guess exact punctuation to find policies
bug.description: Partial title searches fail when the search term is a substring that precedes a comma or semicolon in the policy title. The retrieval system appears to include punctuation in token boundaries, so "Shift Differentials" (without comma) does not match the indexed token "Shift Differentials," (with comma). Adding the trailing comma to the query makes it work, confirming the tokenizer treats punctuation as part of the token rather than a delimiter.

test_case.actual: Correct — chatbot found and summarized the policy
test_case.notes: CRITICAL: Adding the trailing comma made it work. This proves the tokenizer includes commas in tokens.

test_case.notes: "Holiday Premium Pay" appears at the END of the title (no trailing punctuation), so it matches fine

root_cause_analysis.probable_cause:
The search index uses a keyword/hybrid retrieval strategy where the tokenizer (analyzer) does NOT strip punctuation before indexing. As a result: - Indexed token: "Differentials," (with comma) - Query token: "Differentials" (without comma) - These do not match because the comma is part of the indexed token.
This is likely a KEYWORD search issue, not a pure vector/embedding issue. Embeddings are generally punctuation-agnostic, so if retrieval were purely vector-based, this bug would not manifest. The presence of this bug strongly suggests hybrid search (keyword + vector) or a keyword-based title filter.

investigation_checklist.check: Inspect the analyzer/tokenizer configuration on the search index. Is punctuation stripping enabled? What analyzer is used (standard, keyword, custom)? For Azure AI Search: check the analyzer on the "title" and "content" fields.

Determine if retrieval uses hybrid search (keyword + vector) or pure vector. If hybrid: the keyword component is likely the source of punctuation sensitivity. If pure vector: the issue may be in a pre-filter or post-filter on document title.
Check if user queries are normalized (punctuation stripped) before being sent to the search index. If not, this is a quick fix on the query side.

fix.action: Strip commas, semicolons, colons, and common punctuation from user queries before sending to retrieval
fix.pseudocode: import re def normalize_query(query: str) -> str: # Remove commas, semicolons, colons (but preserve hyphens for policy numbers) normalized = re.sub(r'[,;:]+', ' ', query) # Collapse multiple spaces normalized = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', normalized).strip() return normalized

fix.target: Index Analyzer (if query-side fix alone is insufficient)
fix.action: Update the search index analyzer to use a standard analyzer with punctuation filtering
fix.azure_ai_search_example: analyzer: "standard.lucene" OR custom_analyzer: tokenizer: "standard" char_filters: ["punctuation_strip"] token_filters: ["lowercase"]
fix.notes: Changing the analyzer requires re-indexing all documents. Prefer FIX-003-A first.
fix.verification: Index tokens for "Shift Differentials, Weekend..." are ["shift", "differentials", "weekend", ...] without punctuation

fix.action: Strip punctuation from policy titles during ingestion before storing as metadata
fix.notes: This is a belt-and-suspenders approach: normalize BOTH at query time AND at index time

recommendation.title: Implement per-page chunking with overlap
recommendation.description: Chunk each page independently with 100-200 token overlap between consecutive page chunks. Attach page_number, policy_number, policy_title, and section_number metadata to every chunk.

recommendation.title: Build a policy registry / lookup table
recommendation.description: Maintain a small lookup table mapping policy_number → policy_title → filename. Use this for deterministic retrieval when users query by policy number, bypassing semantic search entirely for exact-match scenarios.

recommendation.title: Implement multi-stage retrieval
recommendation.description: Stage 1: Detect policy number in query → metadata filter. Stage 2: Detect policy title keywords → hybrid keyword+vector search. Stage 3: Fall back to pure semantic search if stages 1-2 return no results. This tiered approach handles all three query patterns (number, title, natural language).

recommendation.title: Add query normalization layer
recommendation.description: Before any retrieval: strip punctuation (except hyphens/periods in policy numbers), normalize whitespace, lowercase for keyword matching. This prevents BUG-003 class issues and improves general retrieval robustness.

recommendation.title: Build automated regression test suite
recommendation.description: Create a test harness with the queries from this document. Run automatically after every re-index or pipeline change. Include: - Page 1 retrieval (baseline) - Page 2+ retrieval (BUG-001) - Policy number queries (BUG-002) - Partial title queries without punctuation (BUG-003) - Full title queries (regression) - Contact information extraction - Multi-policy cross-referencing

recommendation.title: Log retrieval misses and zero-result queries
recommendation.description: Track queries where the chatbot returns "Unable to verify," "Not found," or "Outside my scope." Alert when miss rate exceeds threshold. These logs would have caught all 3 bugs before user testing.

recommendation.title: Include section headers in every chunk
recommendation.description: Prepend the policy number, policy title, and current section header to every chunk as a prefix. This improves both semantic similarity (the chunk is self-describing) and keyword matching (section references are always present). Example chunk prefix: "[HR-C 06.00 Time and Attendance Recording — Section 6.03 Supervisor Entry/Editing]"
recommendation.priority: P1 — Significantly improves retrieval quality for all query types

recommendation.title: Improve "not found" responses with suggestions
recommendation.description: When retrieval returns no confident results, instead of "Unable to verify" or "Outside my scope," return: "I couldn't find an exact match. Did you mean one of these policies: [list top 3 closest matches]?" This helps users reformulate queries and reduces dead-end interactions.
